title: Word Ladder
statement: Begin at `begin_word` and change one letter at a time. Every intermediate word must be in `word_list`. Return the number of words in the shortest transformation to `end_word`, counting both ends. Return 0 when no sequence exists.
hints: This is an unweighted graph. An edge joins words at Hamming distance 1. BFS gives the shortest path.
If the end word is not in the list, return 0.
Generating all one-letter neighbors from the alphabet is faster than comparing every pair when the list is long. For short tests either method is fine.

approaches.name: Compare every pair
approaches.explanation: Build the graph explicitly, then BFS.

approaches.name: Wildcard buckets or alphabet expansion
approaches.explanation: BFS without a quadratic graph build.

editorial: Put the word list in a set. BFS from the begin word with distance 1. For each word, try changing every position to every letter. If the new word is in the set, enqueue it with distance + 1 and delete it so it is not visited twice. The first time you generate the end word, return that distance.
